questions.question: The capital of Australia is:
questions.rationale: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne — the world's most famous 'decoy capital' question.

questions.question: The currency of Bhutan is:
questions.rationale: The Bhutanese ngultrum is pegged to the Indian rupee. Kyat belongs to Myanmar, taka to Bangladesh, rufiyaa to the Maldives.

questions.question: Which country's capital is Ankara?
questions.rationale: Ankara became Turkey's capital in 1923; Istanbul is the larger, more famous city — the classic decoy.

questions.question: The official capital of Sri Lanka is:
questions.rationale: The legislative capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte; Colombo remains the commercial capital. Papers phrase it as 'administrative capital' to make Kotte the answer.

questions.question: The currency of Indonesia is:
questions.rationale: Indonesia's rupiah, Malaysia's ringgit, Thailand's baht, Vietnam's dong — four south-east Asian currencies the paper shuffles.

questions.question: South Africa has:
questions.rationale: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial) split the three branches — with Johannesburg as the tempting decoy.

questions.question: The currency of Japan is:
questions.rationale: Yen (Japan), won (Koreas), yuan/renminbi (China) — the three-character east-Asian set every exam recycles.

questions.question: Which of these countries uses the taka?
questions.rationale: The Bangladeshi taka sits in the subcontinental currency ladder with the Nepalese rupee, Pakistani rupee and Afghani.

questions.question: The capital of Canada is:
questions.rationale: Ottawa was chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857, partly as a compromise between Toronto and Montreal — and it remains the answer.

questions.question: Sweden's currency is the:
questions.rationale: Sweden uses the krona; Norway and Denmark use the krone. The single-letter difference is the entire question.
